subject: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
parts:
Hi,

I have a functioning app which works fine locally via runApp() on Windows, as well as on our own hosting of shiny server (Shiny Server v1.0.0.42 and Node.js v0.10.21). I tab through various tabset panels to display different plots without issue. However, on Spark, all tabs remain blank. No plotting occurs. This distinction occurred with version 0.9 but I have upgraded all three to 0.10 and it is the same. Not sure what went wrong because it used to work on Spark as well. It may be related to a supplemental package. I also use shinyAce and shinyRGL.

I noticed with shinyRGL, upon upgrading to shiny version 0.10 I had to move the library(shinyRGL) command from server.R to global.R or the app could not find webGLOutput(). This global placement was not required before. But that was a separate problem. Upon moving that line of code to global.R I was once again able to run the app locally, on our shiny server instance, and on Spark. And this returned me to the original problem of absent plot reactivity on Spark only.

http://spark.rstudio.com/uafsnap/plot3D/
The About tab and the R Code tab work fine. The six plot tabs do nothing. But again, this is only on Spark. They work fine on other systems. I have tried in Firefox and Chrome. Same results. Also, websockets are disabled on our shiny server just like on Spark.

Code is public:
https://github.com/ua-snap/shiny-apps/tree/master/plot3D

Thanks,
Matt

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Re: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
parts:
Also worth noting, in Spark the plot download button still works. It will successfully plot to pdf. The button controls the same plot code which is supposed to be run to generate the browser plot. It's only the browser plots that fail to show on Spark.

Matt

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Re: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
parts:
I have isolated the sources of two confounding problems.

First, it is definitely something with the shinyAce package that no longer is working on Spark, but does work on other systems. Commenting out anything to do with rgl had no effect on any plots, rgl-related or otherwise. Only when I commented out the shinyAce code displays in my main panel 'R Code' tab panel did all the plots begin working again. The app also loads visibly more properly (with shinyAce active, my sidebar input controls flash in 'classic' view, then vanish and properly reappear in 'Selectize' format. This load and reload does not occur with shinyAce code commented out.).

So one problem I need to solve is why I can use shinyAce on our webserver but not on Spark, in the context I am using it. There were prior issues, but they were resolved (it worked with websockets off, so it used to work on Spark where websockets are disabled by default, but not on our own server, until I turned off websockets). Now with websockets off on both servers, it continues to work on our hosted server, but no longer on Spark.

The second issue relates to rgl. Now that I can at least see the plots again with shinyAce code commented out, I can see that all plots work except for rgl which fails to load. Previously, I found instructions to use:
options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) at the top of server.R
to enable rgl to work with Shiny apps. Which it did. Now it must be failing to load for some new reason.

Matt

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Re: Working app, plots do not appear on Spark server
parts:
I've confirmed moving the line:
options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE)
ahead of loading rgl and shinyRGL packages solves my rgl issue just as it seems to have worked here:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/sYxldBUgTxI
RGL plots now show in browser along with all standard (non-rgl) plots.

Only issue that remains is with my use of shinyAce, no plots appear (rgl or standard basic R plots). Plots are still downloadable with a download button in the app, but just don't display in the browser.

Matt
